requirements.quote: Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS complying with the definition of paragraph 2.1. above shall, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges
requirements.text: The AEBS shall meet the performance requirements when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges.

requirements.quote: The effectiveness of AEBS shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields. This shall be demonstrated by compliance
requirements.text: The AEBS shall not have its effectiveness adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields.

requirements.quote: A failure warning when there is a failure in the AEBS that prevents the requirements of this Regulation of being met.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall provide a failure warning when there is a failure in the AEBS that prevents the requirements of this Regulation from being met.

requirements.quote: There shall not be an appreciable time interval between each AEBS self-check, and subsequently there shall not be a delay in illuminating the warning signal
requirements.text: The AEBS shall not have an appreciable time interval between each self-check and shall not delay illuminating the warning signal in the case of an electrically detectable failure.

requirements.quote: Upon detection of any non-electrical failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment), the warning signal as defined in paragraph 5.1.4.1. shall be illuminated
requirements.text: The AEBS shall illuminate the failure warning signal upon detection of any non-electrical failure condition such as sensor blindness or sensor misalignment.

requirements.quote: If the system has not been initialised after a cumulative driving time of 15 seconds above a speed of 10 km/h, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall indicate its non-initialised status to the driver if the system has not been initialised after a cumulative driving time of 15 seconds above a speed of 10 km/h, and this information shall exist until successful initialisation.

requirements.quote: A deactivation warning, if the vehicle is equipped with a means to deactivate the AEBS, shall be given when the system is deactivated.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall give a deactivation warning when the system is deactivated, where the vehicle is equipped with a means to deactivate the AEBS.

requirements.quote: the system shall provide emergency braking interventions described in paragraphs 5.2.1.2. and 5.2.2.2. having the purpose of significantly decreasing the speed of the subject vehicle
requirements.text: The AEBS shall provide emergency braking interventions having the purpose of significantly decreasing the speed of the subject vehicle.

requirements.quote: The system shall be designed to minimise the generation of collision warning signals and to avoid advanced emergency braking in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall be designed to minimise the generation of collision warning signals and to avoid emergency braking in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision.

requirements.quote: Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS shall meet the performance requirements of UN Regulation No. 13 in its 11 series of amendments for vehicles of Category M2, M3, N2, N3 and shall be equipped with an anti-lock system
requirements.text: The vehicle fitted with the AEBS shall be equipped with an anti-lock system in accordance with the performance requirements of Annex 13 to UN Regulation No. 13 in its 11 series of amendments.

requirements.quote: When an imminent collision, with a preceding vehicle of Category M, N or O, is detected in the same lane with a relative speed above that speed up to which the subject vehicle is able to avoid the collision
requirements.text: The AEBS shall provide a collision warning when an imminent collision with a preceding vehicle of Category M, N or O is detected in the same lane with a relative speed above that speed up to which the subject vehicle is able to avoid the collision, within the conditions specified in paragraph 5.2.1.4.

requirements.quote: a collision warning shall be provided as specified in paragraph 5.5.1., and shall be triggered at the latest 0.8 seconds before the start of emergency braking
requirements.text: The collision warning shall be triggered at the latest 0.8 seconds before the start of emergency braking.

requirements.quote: in case the collision cannot be anticipated in time to give a collision warning 0.8 seconds ahead of an emergency braking, a collision warning as specified in paragraph 5.5.1. shall be provided no later than the start of the emergency braking
requirements.text: Where the collision cannot be anticipated in time to give a collision warning 0.8 seconds ahead of emergency braking, the AEBS shall provide the collision warning no later than the start of the emergency braking.

requirements.quote: When the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision, there shall be a braking demand of at least 4 m/s² to the service braking system of the vehicle.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall issue a braking demand of at least 4 m/s² to the service braking system of the vehicle when it has detected the possibility of an imminent collision.

requirements.quote: The emergency braking may be aborted, or the deceleration demand reduced below the threshold above (as relevant), if the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present or the risk of a collision has decreased.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall abort the emergency braking or reduce the deceleration demand below the threshold where the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present or the risk of a collision has decreased.

requirements.quote: The system shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 10 km/h and the maximum design speed of the vehicle and at all vehicle load conditions
requirements.text: The AEBS shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 10 km/h and the maximum design speed of the vehicle and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.

requirements.quote: In absence of driver’s input which would lead to interruption according to paragraph 5.3.2., the AEBS shall be able to achieve a relative impact speed that is less or equal to the maximum relative impact speed as shown in the following table
requirements.text: The AEBS shall, in absence of driver's input leading to interruption, achieve a relative impact speed less than or equal to the maximum relative impact speed shown in Table 1.

requirements.quote: Table 1 Maximum relative Impact Speed (km/h) (regardless whether target stationary or moving)*
requirements.text: For an N2 vehicle with a maximum mass above 8 t and pneumatic braking, the AEBS shall achieve a maximum relative impact speed of 0 km/h at relative speeds of 10 to 60 km/h, 25 km/h at 70 km/h and 37 km/h at 80 km/h.

requirements.quote: When conditions deviate from those listed above, the system shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy when conditions deviate from those listed in paragraph 5.2.1.4.

requirements.quote: Notwithstanding the table above, for those vehicles driving in urban areas where the speed is limited to 60kph or below, the speed reduction shall be at least 40 km/h
requirements.text: Where the vehicle is driven in urban areas where the speed is limited to 60 km/h or below, the AEBS shall provide a speed reduction of at least 40 km/h.

requirements.quote: When the AEBS has detected the possibility of a collision with a pedestrian crossing the road at a constant speed of not more than 5 km/h, within the conditions specified in paragraph 5.2.2.4., a collision warning as specified in paragraph 5.5.1. shall be provided no later than the start of the emergency braking
requirements.text: The AEBS shall provide a collision warning no later than the start of the emergency braking when it has detected the possibility of a collision with a pedestrian crossing the road at a constant speed of not more than 5 km/h within the conditions specified in paragraph 5.2.2.4.

requirements.quote: When the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision, there shall be a braking demand of at least 4 m/s² to the service braking system of the vehicle.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall issue a braking demand of at least 4 m/s² to the service braking system of the vehicle when the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision with a pedestrian.

requirements.quote: The system shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 20 km/h and 60 km/h and at all vehicle load conditions., unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 20 km/h and 60 km/h and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.

requirements.quote: Maximum Impact Speed in the direction of travel of the vehicle (km/h) *
requirements.text: For an N2 vehicle with a maximum mass above 8 t and pneumatic braking, the AEBS shall achieve a maximum impact speed in the direction of travel of 0 km/h at 20 km/h subject speed, 13 km/h at 26 km/h, 18 km/h at 30 km/h, 29 km/h at 40 km/h, 39 km/h at 50 km/h and 49 km/h at 60 km/h.

requirements.quote: The AEBS shall provide appropriate and robust means for the driver to interrupt the collision warning and the emergency braking.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall provide appropriate and robust means for the driver to interrupt the collision warning and the emergency braking.

requirements.quote: In both cases above, this interruption may be initiated by any positive action (e.g. kick-down or a swerving action that results in enough change of direction to not hit the target)
requirements.text: The AEBS shall allow interruption of the collision warning and emergency braking by any positive action such as kick-down or a swerving action resulting in enough change of direction to not hit the target.

requirements.quote: The AEBS function shall be automatically reinstated at each initiation of the powertrain
requirements.text: The AEBS function shall be automatically reinstated at each initiation of the powertrain where a means to manually deactivate the AEBS function is provided.

requirements.quote: The AEBS deactivation control shall be designed a in such a way that manual deactivation shall not be possible with less than two deliberate actions.
requirements.text: The AEBS deactivation control shall be designed so that manual deactivation is not possible with less than two deliberate actions.

requirements.quote: For every manual deactivation requested by the driver as referenced in paragraph 5.4.1.2., AEBS shall be automatically reinstated latest after 15 minutes.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall be automatically reinstated latest after 15 minutes for every manual deactivation requested by the driver, and it shall be possible for the driver to reactivate it at any time including whilst driving.

requirements.quote: A constant optical warning signal shall inform the driver that the AEBS function has been deactivated.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall inform the driver with a constant optical warning signal that the AEBS function has been deactivated.

requirements.quote: The collision warning referred to in paragraphs 5.2.1.1. and 5.2.2.1. shall be provided by at least two modes selected from acoustic, haptic or optical.
requirements.text: The collision warning shall be provided by at least two modes selected from acoustic, haptic or optical.

requirements.quote: Where an optical means is used as part of the collision warning. the optical signal may be the flashing of the failure warning signal
requirements.text: Where an optical means is used as part of the collision warning, the optical signal may be the flashing of the failure warning signal specified in paragraph 5.5.4.

requirements.quote: The failure warning referred to in paragraph 5.1.4.1. shall be a constant yellow optical warning signal.
requirements.text: The AEBS failure warning shall be a constant yellow optical warning signal.

requirements.quote: Each AEBS optical warning signal shall be activated either when the ignition (start) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or when the ignition (start) switch is in a position between the "on" (run) and "start" position
requirements.text: Each AEBS optical warning signal shall be activated when the ignition switch is turned to the on (run) position or to the check position between on and start.

requirements.quote: The optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight; the satisfactory condition of the signals must be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.
requirements.text: The AEBS optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight and their satisfactory condition shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.

requirements.quote: When the driver is provided with an optical warning signal to indicate that the AEBS is temporarily not available, for example due to inclement weather conditions, the signal shall be constant.
requirements.text: The optical warning signal indicating that the AEBS is temporarily not available, for example due to inclement weather conditions, shall be constant.

requirements.quote: At a Periodic Technical Inspection, it shall be possible to confirm the correct operational status of the AEBS by a visible observation of the failure warning signal status. following a "power-ON" and any bulb check.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall allow confirmation of its correct operational status at a Periodic Technical Inspection by visible observation of the failure warning signal status following a power-ON and any bulb check.

requirements.quote: The test shall be performed on a flat, dry, concrete or asphalt road affording good adhesion.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall be tested on a flat, dry, concrete or asphalt road affording good adhesion.

requirements.quote: The ambient temperature shall be between 0°C and 45°C.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall be tested at an ambient temperature between 0 °C and 45 °C.

requirements.quote: Natural ambient illumination must be homogeneous in the test area and in excess of 1000 lux in the case of vehicle to vehicle scenario
requirements.text: The AEBS vehicle-to-vehicle tests shall be performed at a homogeneous natural ambient illumination in excess of 1000 lux, and vehicle-to-pedestrian tests in excess of 2000 lux.

requirements.quote: During the series of test runs, the fuel level may decrease but shall never fall below 50 per cent.
requirements.text: The AEBS test vehicle shall maintain a fuel level never below 50 per cent during the series of test runs.

requirements.quote: The average temperature of the service brakes on the hottest axle of the vehicle, measured inside the brake linings or on the braking path of the disc or drum, is below 100°C prior to each test run.
requirements.text: The service brakes of the AEBS test vehicle shall be below 100 °C on the hottest axle prior to each test run.

requirements.quote: The target used for the vehicle detection tests shall be a regular high-volume series production passenger car of Category M1 or alternatively a "soft target" representative of a passenger vehicle
requirements.text: The vehicle target used for the AEBS vehicle detection tests shall be a regular high-volume series production passenger car of Category M1 or a soft target representative of a passenger vehicle according to ISO 19206-3:2021.

requirements.quote: The target used for the pedestrian detection tests shall be a child "articulated soft target" and be representative of the human attributes applicable to the sensor system of the AEBS under test according to ISO 19206-2:2018.
requirements.text: The target used for the AEBS pedestrian detection tests shall be a child articulated soft target representative of the human attributes applicable to the sensor system according to ISO 19206-2:2018.

requirements.quote: The subject vehicle shall approach the stationary target in a straight line for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with a subject vehicle to target centreline offset of not more than 0.2 m.
requirements.text: The AEBS test vehicle shall approach the stationary target in a straight line for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with a subject vehicle to target centreline offset of not more than 0.2 m.

requirements.quote: Tests shall be conducted with a vehicle travelling at the following speeds, with a tolerance of +/- 2 km/h, but not beyond the range specified in paragraph 5.2.1.3., for all tests:
requirements.text: The AEBS stationary vehicle target tests shall be conducted at 20 km/h, at the maximum required impact avoidance speed and at that speed plus 8 km/h or the maximum design speed, whichever is lower, with a tolerance of ± 2 km/h.

requirements.quote: A distance corresponding to a Time To Collision (TTC) of at least 4 seconds from the target.
requirements.text: The functional part of the stationary vehicle target test shall start at a distance corresponding to a time to collision of at least 4 seconds from the target.

requirements.quote: The subject vehicle and the moving target shall travel in a straight line, in the same direction, for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test. with a subject vehicle to target centreline offset of not more than 0.2m.
requirements.text: The AEBS moving vehicle target test shall be performed with the subject vehicle and the moving target travelling in a straight line in the same direction for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with a centreline offset of not more than 0.2 m.

requirements.quote: and a target travelling at 20 km/h, with a tolerance of +0/-2 km/h for both the target and the subject vehicles
requirements.text: The moving target in the AEBS moving vehicle target test shall travel at 20 km/h with a tolerance of +0/-2 km/h.

requirements.quote: The pedestrian target shall travel in a straight line perpendicular to the subject vehicle’s direction of travel at a constant speed of 5 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h, starting not before the functional part of the test has started.
requirements.text: The pedestrian target shall travel in a straight line perpendicular to the subject vehicle's direction of travel at a constant speed of 5 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h, starting not before the functional part of the test has started.

requirements.quote: The pedestrian target’s positioning shall be coordinated with the subject vehicle in such a way that the impact point of the pedestrian target on the front of the subject vehicle is on the longitudinal centreline of the subject vehicle with a tolerance of not more than 0.1 m
requirements.text: The pedestrian target shall be positioned so that its impact point on the front of the subject vehicle is on the longitudinal centreline with a tolerance of not more than 0.1 m if the subject vehicle would remain at the prescribed test speed and not brake.

requirements.quote: Tests shall be conducted with a vehicle travelling at the following speeds, with a tolerance of +/- 2 km/h for all tests, but not beyond the range specified in paragraph 5.2.2.3.:
requirements.text: The AEBS pedestrian tests shall be conducted at 20 km/h, at the maximum required collision avoidance speed and at that speed plus 8 km/h or the maximum design speed, whichever is lower, with a tolerance of ± 2 km/h.

requirements.quote: Simulate an electrical failure, for example, by disconnecting the power source to any AEBS component or disconnecting any electrical connection between AEBS components.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall be subjected to a simulated electrical failure by disconnecting the power source to any AEBS component or any electrical connection between AEBS components.

requirements.quote: The failure warning signal mentioned in paragraph 5.5.4. above shall be activated and remain activated not later than 10 s after the vehicle has been driven at a speed greater than 10 km/h
requirements.text: The AEBS failure warning signal shall be activated and remain activated not later than 10 s after the vehicle has been driven at a speed greater than 10 km/h following a simulated failure.

requirements.quote: turn the ignition (start) switch to the "on" (run) position and deactivate the AEBS. The warning signal mentioned in paragraph 5.4.4. above shall be activated.
requirements.text: The AEBS deactivation warning signal shall be activated when the AEBS is deactivated with the ignition switch in the on (run) position.

requirements.quote: Any of the above test scenarios, where a scenario describes one test setup at one subject vehicle speed at one load condition of one category
requirements.text: Each AEBS test scenario shall be performed two times, and a scenario shall be accounted as passed if the required performance is met in two test runs.

requirements.quote: The number of failed tests runs within one category shall not exceed: (a) 10.0 per cent of the performed test runs for the Vehicle to Vehicle tests
requirements.text: The number of failed test runs within the Vehicle to Vehicle category shall not exceed 10.0 per cent of the performed test runs.

requirements.quote: The subject vehicle shall travel for a distance of at least 60 m, at a constant speed of 50 ± 2 km/h to pass centrally between the two stationary vehicles.
requirements.text: The AEBS false reaction test vehicle shall travel for a distance of at least 60 m at a constant speed of 50 ± 2 km/h to pass centrally between the two stationary vehicles.

requirements.quote: The AEBS shall not provide a collision warning and shall not initiate the emergency braking phase.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall not provide a collision warning and shall not initiate the emergency braking phase when passing between two stationary vehicles in the false reaction test.

requirements.quote: at least 30 per cent* of required tests shall be performed physically including at least one test of each scenario variant described in paragraphs 6.4 to 6.6 relevant for the approval
requirements.text: At least 30 per cent of the required AEBS tests shall be performed physically, including at least one test of each scenario variant described in paragraphs 6.4 to 6.6 relevant for the approval.

requirements.quote: The above approval mark affixed to a vehicle shows that the vehicle type concerned has been approved in Belgium (E 6) with regard to the Advanced Emergency Braking Systems (AEBS)
requirements.text: The AEBS shall bear the approval mark showing the circle surrounding the letter E, the Regulation number followed by R and the approval number, with C for Vehicle to Vehicle and P for Vehicle to Pedestrian.

requirements.quote: Each unit shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.
requirements.text: Each AEBS unit shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content.

requirements.quote: The identification defines the hardware and software version and, where the latter changes such as to alter the function of the unit as far as this Regulation is concerned, this identification shall also be changed.
requirements.text: The AEBS unit identification shall define the hardware and software version and shall be changed where the software changes alter the function of the unit.

requirements.quote: The Manufacturer shall provide a statement which affirms that the strategy chosen to achieve "The System" objectives will not, under non-fault conditions, prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall be designed with a strategy that will not, under non-fault conditions, prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle.

requirements.quote: In case of a failure, the driver shall be warned for example by warning signal or message display.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall warn the driver by warning signal or message display in case of a failure.

requirements.quote: the warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists
requirements.text: The AEBS failure warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists when the system is not deactivated by the driver.

requirements.quote: If the chosen provision selects the removal of the Higher Level Function, all the corresponding output control signals associated with this function shall be inhibited, and in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.
requirements.text: Where the AEBS safety concept removes the higher level function, all its corresponding output control signals shall be inhibited in a manner that limits the transition disturbance.

requirements.quote: This documentation shall describe the measures in place to ensure the "The System" does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when the performance of "The System" is affected by environmental conditions
requirements.text: The AEBS shall be provided with measures ensuring it does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when its performance is affected by environmental conditions such as climatic, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress or ice packing.

requirements.quote: The following scenarios shall be used to assess the system’s strategies implemented in order to minimize the generation of false reactions.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall implement strategies to minimise false reactions, assessed against the scenarios of Appendix 2 to Annex 3.

requirements.quote: The subject vehicle drives at a speed of 30 km/h (with a tolerance of +0/-2 km/h) toward the intersection, and decelerates by braking to a speed of not less than 16 km/h at a point where the subject vehicle begins to steer left / right
requirements.text: The AEBS shall not generate a false reaction when the subject vehicle drives at 30 km/h toward an intersection and decelerates to not less than 16 km/h where it begins to steer left or right in front of an oncoming vehicle.

requirements.quote: the speed of the subject vehicle is not less than 26 km/h and the TTC to the frontal vehicle is not more than 4.7 seconds
requirements.text: The AEBS shall not generate a false reaction when a forward vehicle turning right or left leaves the lane and the subject vehicle speed is not less than 26 km/h with a time to collision to the frontal vehicle of not more than 4.7 seconds.

requirements.quote: The subject vehicle drives at a speed of 30 (with a tolerance of +0/-2 km/h) km/h toward the curve of which the radius is not more than 25 m at the outer side of the road
requirements.text: The AEBS shall not generate a false reaction when the subject vehicle drives at 30 km/h toward a curve of radius not more than 25 m with guard pipes and a stationary object just outside the guard pipes.

requirements.quote: The subject vehicle drives a straight road at a speed of 40 km/h (with a tolerance of +0/-2 km/h) and begins to steer in order to change the lane in front of the signboard which notifies reducing the lane.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall not generate a false reaction when the subject vehicle drives at 40 km/h and begins to steer to change lane in front of a signboard notifying a lane reduction.

requirements.quote: Credibility of the toolchain that is used for the virtual testing shall be demonstrated by the vehicle manufacturer to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service.
requirements.text: Where virtual testing is used for the AEBS, the credibility of the toolchain shall be demonstrated considering capability, accuracy, correctness, fit for purpose and usability.

requirements.quote: The toolchain and its components shall be capable of accurately representing the relevant aspects of the physical AEBS that is being modelled.
requirements.text: The virtual testing toolchain and its components shall be capable of accurately representing the relevant aspects of the physical AEBS being modelled.

requirements.quote: The braking equipment shall be so designed, constructed and fitted as to enable the vehicle in normal use, despite the vibration to which it may be subjected, to comply with the provisions of this Regulation.
requirements.text: The AEBS service brake interface shall be so designed, constructed and fitted as to enable the vehicle in normal use, despite vibration, to comply with the braking requirements.

requirements.quote: In particular, the braking equipment shall be so designed, constructed and fitted as to be able to resist the corroding and ageing phenomena to which it is exposed.
requirements.text: The braking equipment actuated by the AEBS shall be so designed, constructed and fitted as to resist the corroding and ageing phenomena to which it is exposed.

requirements.quote: Brake linings shall not contain asbestos.
requirements.text: The brake linings of the vehicle fitted with the AEBS shall not contain asbestos.

requirements.quote: The effectiveness of the braking equipment shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields.
requirements.text: The effectiveness of the braking equipment commanded by the AEBS shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields, demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements of Regulation No. 10.

requirements.quote: A failure detection signal may interrupt momentarily (< 10 ms) the demand signal in the control transmission, provided that the braking performance is thereby not reduced.
requirements.text: A failure detection signal of the AEBS may interrupt momentarily (< 10 ms) the demand signal in the control transmission only if the braking performance is thereby not reduced.

requirements.quote: The service braking system shall make it possible to control the movement of the vehicle and to halt it safely, speedily and effectively, whatever its speed and load, on any up or down gradient.
requirements.text: The service braking system commanded by the AEBS shall make it possible to control the movement of the vehicle and halt it safely, speedily and effectively whatever its speed and load on any up or down gradient.

requirements.quote: The secondary braking system shall make it possible by application of the service brake control to halt the vehicle within a reasonable distance in the event of failure of the service braking system.
requirements.text: The secondary braking system shall halt the vehicle within a reasonable distance by application of the service brake control in the event of failure of the service braking system.

requirements.quote: It shall be possible to assess the wear condition of the components of the service brake that are subject to wear e.g. friction linings and drums/discs
requirements.text: The service brake components commanded by the AEBS shall allow assessment of their wear condition, for friction linings and drums/discs, at periodic technical inspection.

requirements.quote: It shall be possible to generate maximum braking forces under static conditions on a rolling road or roller brake tester.
requirements.text: The braking system commanded by the AEBS shall allow generation of maximum braking forces under static conditions on a rolling road or roller brake tester.

requirements.quote: The effectiveness of the linkage between the control of the service braking system and the different components of the transmission systems shall not be liable to diminish after a certain period of use.
requirements.text: The effectiveness of the linkage between the service brake control and the transmission components shall not diminish after a certain period of use.

requirements.quote: in the event of breakage of any component other than the brakes (as defined in paragraph 2.6. above) and the components referred to in paragraph 5.2.2.10. below, or of any other failure of the service braking system
requirements.text: That part of the service braking system not affected by a single failure shall be able to bring the vehicle to a halt in the conditions prescribed for secondary braking.

requirements.quote: Any such part as aforesaid whose failure would make it impossible to brake the vehicle with a degree of effectiveness at least equal to that prescribed for secondary braking shall be made of metal or of a material with equivalent characteristics
requirements.text: Components of the service brake control whose failure would prevent secondary braking shall be made of metal or of a material with equivalent characteristics and shall not undergo notable distortion in normal operation.

requirements.quote: The failure of a part of a hydraulic transmission system shall be signalled to the driver by a device comprising a red tell-tale signal lighting up before or upon application of a differential pressure of not more than 15.5 bar
requirements.text: The AEBS hydraulic brake interface shall signal a failure of a hydraulic transmission part to the driver by a red tell-tale lighting up before or upon application of a differential pressure of not more than 15.5 bar.

requirements.quote: The tell-tale signal shall be visible even by daylight; the satisfactory condition of the signal shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.
requirements.text: The brake failure tell-tale signal shall be visible even by daylight and its satisfactory condition easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.

requirements.quote: Intrinsic variations in the torque output of the electrical regenerative braking system (e.g. as a result of changes in the electric state of charge in the traction batteries) are automatically compensated by appropriate variation in the phasing relationship
requirements.text: Any intrinsic variations in the torque output of a regenerative braking system shall be automatically compensated so that the braking rate remains related to the driver's braking demand.

requirements.quote: The action of the service braking system shall be distributed between the wheels of one and the same axle symmetrically in relation to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
requirements.text: The action of the service braking system commanded by the AEBS shall be distributed between the wheels of one and the same axle symmetrically in relation to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.

requirements.quote: Compensation by the electric control transmission for deterioration or defect within the braking system shall be indicated to the driver by means of the yellow warning signal specified in paragraph 5.2.21.1.2. below.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall indicate compensation by the electric control transmission for deterioration or defect within the braking system to the driver by means of the yellow warning signal when the compensation exceeds the specified limits.

requirements.quote: Malfunctions of the electric control transmission shall not apply the brakes contrary to the intentions of the driver or ADS.
requirements.text: Malfunctions of the electric control transmission shall not apply the brakes contrary to the intentions of the driver.

requirements.quote: Wear of the brakes shall be capable of being easily taken up by means of a system of manual or automatic adjustment.
requirements.text: The brakes commanded by the AEBS shall have wear capable of being easily taken up by a system of manual or automatic adjustment, with sufficient reserve of travel.

requirements.quote: Wear adjustment shall be automatic for the service brakes. Automatic wear adjustment devices shall be such that after heating followed by cooling of the brakes, effective braking is still ensured.
requirements.text: Wear adjustment shall be automatic for the service brakes, and effective braking shall still be ensured after heating followed by cooling of the brakes.

requirements.quote: It shall be possible to easily assess this wear on service brake linings from the outside or underside of the vehicle, without the removal of the wheels, by the provision of appropriate inspection holes or by some other means.
requirements.text: The wear of service brake linings shall be easily assessable from the outside or underside of the vehicle without removal of the wheels by appropriate inspection holes or by some other means.

requirements.quote: a sensing device per wheel (twin wheels are considered as a single wheel), which will warn the driver at his driving position when lining replacement is necessary, is acceptable
requirements.text: The AEBS vehicle shall be fitted with a sensing device per wheel warning the driver at his driving position when lining replacement is necessary, or with inspection holes allowing wear assessment.

requirements.quote: The type of fluid to be used in hydraulic transmission braking systems shall be identified by the symbol in accordance with Figure 1 or 2 of Standard ISO 9128:2006 and the appropriate DOT marking (e.g. DOT 3).
requirements.text: The hydraulic transmission braking system shall identify the type of fluid by the ISO 9128:2006 symbol and the appropriate DOT marking affixed visibly and indelibly within 100 mm of the filling ports.

requirements.quote: Any vehicle fitted with a service brake actuated from an energy reserve shall, where the prescribed secondary braking performance cannot be obtained by means of this braking system without the use of the stored energy, be provided with a warning device
requirements.text: The AEBS vehicle with a service brake actuated from an energy reserve shall be provided with a warning device giving an optical or acoustic signal at the latest when the stored energy falls to the specified level.

requirements.quote: This warning device shall be directly and permanently connected to the circuit. The red warning signal specified in paragraph 5.2.21.1.1. shall be used as the optical warning signal.
requirements.text: The energy reserve warning device shall be directly and permanently connected to the circuit and use the red warning signal specified in paragraph 5.2.21.1.1. as its optical signal.

requirements.quote: where an auxiliary source of energy is essential to the functioning of a braking system, the reserve of energy shall be such as to ensure that, if the engine stops or in the event of a failure of the means by which the energy source is driven, the braking performance remains adequate to bring the vehicle to a halt
requirements.text: The AEBS braking system shall have an energy reserve ensuring that, if the engine stops or the means driving the energy source fails, the braking performance remains adequate to bring the vehicle to a halt.

requirements.quote: The pneumatic/hydraulic/electrical auxiliary equipment shall be supplied with energy in such a way that during its operation, the prescribed deceleration values can be reached
requirements.text: The auxiliary equipment supplied from the same energy source as the braking system shall be supplied with energy such that the prescribed deceleration values can be reached during its operation.

requirements.quote: In the case of a single temporary failure (< 40 ms) within the electric control transmission, excluding its energy supply, (e.g. non-transmitted signal or data error) there shall be no distinguishable effect on the service braking performance.
requirements.text: The AEBS vehicle shall have no distinguishable effect on the service braking performance in the case of a single temporary failure (< 40 ms) within the electric control transmission excluding its energy supply.

requirements.quote: A failure within the electric control transmission,5 not including its energy reserve, that affects the function and performance of systems addressed in this Regulation shall be indicated to the driver by the red or yellow warning signal
requirements.text: A failure within the electric control transmission not including its energy reserve that affects the function and performance of the braking system shall be indicated to the driver by the red or yellow warning signal as appropriate.

requirements.quote: When the battery voltage falls below a value nominated by the manufacturer at which the prescribed service braking performance can no longer be guaranteed the red warning signal specified in paragraph 5.2.21.1.1. below shall be activated.
requirements.text: The red warning signal shall be activated when the battery voltage falls below the manufacturer-nominated value at which the prescribed service braking performance can no longer be guaranteed.

requirements.quote: A red warning signal, indicating failures defined elsewhere in this Regulation within the vehicle braking equipment which preclude achievement of the prescribed service braking performance
requirements.text: The AEBS shall provide a red warning signal indicating failures within the vehicle braking equipment which preclude achievement of the prescribed service braking performance or functioning of at least one of two independent service braking circuits.

requirements.quote: Where applicable, a yellow warning signal indicating an electrically detected defect within the vehicle braking equipment, which is not indicated by the red warning signal
requirements.text: The AEBS shall provide a yellow warning signal indicating an electrically detected defect within the vehicle braking equipment which is not indicated by the red warning signal.

requirements.quote: The warning signals required by this paragraph shall employ the brake system malfunction symbol listed in UN Regulation No. 121.
requirements.text: The brake failure and defect warning signals shall employ the brake system malfunction symbol listed in UN Regulation No. 121.

requirements.quote: The warning signals shall be visible, even by daylight; the satisfactory condition of the signals shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat; the failure of a component of the warning devices shall not entail any loss of the braking system's performance.
requirements.text: The brake warning signals shall be visible even by daylight and easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat, and failure of a warning device component shall not entail loss of braking system performance.

requirements.quote: A specified failure or defect shall be signalled to the driver by the above-mentioned warning signal(s) not later than on actuation of the relevant braking control;
requirements.text: A specified failure or defect shall be signalled to the driver by the warning signal not later than on actuation of the relevant braking control.

requirements.quote: The warning signal(s) shall remain displayed as long as the failure/defect persists and the ignition (start) switch is in the "On" (run) position;
requirements.text: The brake warning signal shall remain displayed as long as the failure or defect persists and the ignition switch is in the On (run) position.

requirements.quote: The warning signal shall be constant (not flashing).
requirements.text: The brake warning signal shall be constant and not flashing.

requirements.quote: The warning signal(s) mentioned above shall light up when the electrical equipment of the vehicle (and the braking system) is energised.
requirements.text: The brake warning signals shall light up when the electrical equipment of the vehicle and the braking system is energised, and the system shall verify before extinguishing the signals that none of the specified failures or defects are present.

requirements.quote: Deceleration demanded by an Automated Driving System, automatically commanded braking and/or regenerative braking
requirements.text: The AEBS shall generate the stop lamp signal when the braking it commands exceeds 1.3 m/s², and this signal shall be kept as long as a deceleration demand persists.

requirements.quote: An appropriate measure (e.g. switch-off-hysteresis, averaging, time delay) shall be implemented in order to avoid fast changes of the signal resulting in flickering of the stop lamps.
requirements.text: The AEBS shall implement an appropriate measure such as switch-off-hysteresis, averaging or time delay to avoid fast changes of the stop lamp signal causing flicker.

requirements.quote: Activation of part of the service braking system by "selective braking" or by functions whose primary intention is not to decelerate the vehicle (e.g. slight actuation of the friction brakes to clean the discs) shall not generate the signal
requirements.text: Activation of part of the service braking system by selective braking or by functions whose primary intention is not to decelerate the vehicle shall not generate the stop lamp signal.

requirements.quote: The signal shall not be activated when the vehicle deceleration is below 6 m/s² but it may be generated at any deceleration at or above this value
requirements.text: The emergency braking signal shall not be activated when the vehicle deceleration is below 6 m/s² but may be generated at any deceleration at or above this value.

requirements.quote: The signal shall be de-activated at the latest when the deceleration has fallen below 2.5 m/s².
requirements.text: The emergency braking signal shall be de-activated at the latest when the deceleration has fallen below 2.5 m/s².

requirements.quote: Whilst the ADS is active, detected faults as specified in this UN Regulation shall be transmitted to the ADS.
requirements.text: The braking system shall transmit detected faults to the automated driving system whilst the ADS is active.

requirements.quote: The above approval mark affixed to a vehicle shows that the vehicle type concerned has, with regard to braking, been approved in the United Kingdom (E 11) pursuant to Regulation No. 13-H under approval number 012439.
requirements.text: The vehicle shall bear the braking approval mark with a minimum dimension a = 8 mm showing the circle with the letter E, the Regulation number followed by R and the approval number.

requirements.quote: At the start of the tests, the tyres shall be cold and at the pressure prescribed for the load actually borne by the wheels when the vehicle is stationary;
requirements.text: The AEBS braking tests shall start with cold tyres at the pressure prescribed for the load actually borne by the wheels.

requirements.quote: The prescribed performance shall be obtained without locking of the wheels at speeds exceeding 15 km/h, without deviation of the vehicle from a 3.5 m wide lane, without exceeding a yaw angle of 15° and without abnormal vibrations;
requirements.text: The AEBS shall achieve the prescribed braking performance without wheel locking at speeds exceeding 15 km/h, without deviation from a 3.5 m wide lane, without exceeding a yaw angle of 15° and without abnormal vibrations.

requirements.quote: The average temperature of the service brakes on the hottest axle of the vehicle, measured inside the brake linings or on the braking path of the disc or drum, is between 65 and 100 °C prior to any brake application.
requirements.text: The service brakes shall be between 65 and 100 °C on the hottest axle prior to any brake application in the Type-0 test.

requirements.quote: The vehicle shall be laden, the distribution of its mass among the axles being that stated by the manufacturer
requirements.text: The AEBS Type-0 test shall be conducted with the vehicle laden and its mass distributed among the axles as stated by the manufacturer.

requirements.quote: The service brakes of all vehicles shall be tested by successively applying and releasing the brakes a number of times, the vehicle being laden
requirements.text: The service brakes shall be tested in the Type-I fade test by successively applying and releasing the brakes 15 times with the vehicle laden at 80 per cent of maximum speed, not exceeding 120 km/h, with a cycle duration of 45 s.

requirements.quote: In these tests, the force applied to the control shall be so adjusted as to attain a mean deceleration of 3 m/s2 during every brake application
requirements.text: The control force in the Type-I heating procedure shall be adjusted to attain a mean deceleration of 3 m/s² during every brake application.

requirements.quote: This hot performance shall not be less than 752 per cent of that prescribed, nor less than 60 per cent of the figure recorded in the Type-0 test with the engine disconnected.
requirements.text: The hot performance of the service braking system shall not be less than 60 per cent of the figure recorded in the Type-0 test with the engine disconnected.

requirements.quote: This recovery performance shall not be less than 70 per cent, nor more than 150 per cent, of the figure recorded in the Type-0 test with the engine disconnected.
requirements.text: The recovery performance of the service braking system shall not be less than 70 per cent nor more than 150 per cent of the figure recorded in the Type-0 test with the engine disconnected.

requirements.quote: The service brakes shall be tested under the conditions shown in the following table:
requirements.text: The service brakes shall achieve at the Type-0 test with engine disconnected a stopping distance of not more than 0.1 v + 0.0060 v² and a mean fully developed deceleration of at least 6.43 m/s² from 100 km/h.

requirements.quote: The secondary braking system shall give a stopping distance not exceeding the following value: 0.1 v + 0.0158 v2 (m) and a mean fully developed deceleration not less than 2.44 m/s2
requirements.text: The secondary braking system shall give a stopping distance not exceeding 0.1 v + 0.0158 v² and a mean fully developed deceleration not less than 2.44 m/s².

requirements.quote: The parking braking system shall be capable of holding the laden vehicle stationary on a 20 per cent up or down gradient.
requirements.text: The parking braking system shall hold the laden vehicle stationary on a 20 per cent up or down gradient.

requirements.quote: If the control device is manual, the force applied to it shall not exceed 40 daN.
requirements.text: Where the parking brake control device is manual, the force applied to it shall not exceed 40 daN.

requirements.quote: If it is a foot control device, the force exerted on the control shall not exceed 50 daN.
requirements.text: Where the parking brake control device is a foot control, the force exerted on the control shall not exceed 50 daN.

requirements.quote: In an emergency manoeuvre, the time elapsing between the moment when the control device begins to be actuated and the moment when the braking force on the least favourable placed axle reaches the level corresponding to the prescribed performance shall not exceed 0.6 seconds;
requirements.text: In an emergency manoeuvre, the time between actuation of the control device and the braking force on the least favourable placed axle reaching the level corresponding to the prescribed performance shall not exceed 0.6 seconds.

requirements.quote: After eight full-stroke actuations of the service brake control, it shall still be possible to achieve, on the ninth application, the performance prescribed for the secondary braking system.
requirements.text: The hydraulic braking system with stored energy shall still achieve, on the ninth application after eight full-stroke actuations, the performance prescribed for the secondary braking system.

requirements.quote: In the case of all vehicles, the time t shall not exceed 20 seconds.
requirements.text: The time for the pressure in the energy storage device to rise from p2 to p1 without brake application shall not exceed 20 seconds.

requirements.quote: The performance of the electrical storage device(s) shall be such that, as a minimum, after eight full actuations of the service braking system control (as described in paragraph 1.2.3.3. below) the performance (at the ninth braking) at least fulfils the requirements specified for secondary braking.
requirements.text: The electrical storage devices of the braking system shall, after eight full actuations of the service brake control, achieve at the ninth braking at least the performance specified for secondary braking.

requirements.quote: For all states of load of the vehicle, the adhesion utilization curve of the rear axle shall not be situated above that for the front axle:
requirements.text: For all states of load of the vehicle, the adhesion utilization curve of the rear axle shall not be situated above that of the front axle for all braking rates between 0.15 and 0.8.

requirements.quote: For k values between 0.2 and 0.82: z ≥ 0.1 + 0.7 (k - 0.2)
requirements.text: The vehicle shall satisfy the condition z ≥ 0.1 + 0.7 (k − 0.2) for k values between 0.2 and 0.82.

requirements.quote: it shall be possible, in the event of the failure of its control, (e.g. by disconnecting the control linkage), to stop the vehicle under the conditions of the Type-0 test with the engine disconnected to give a stopping distance not exceeding 0.1 v + 0.0100 v2 (m)
requirements.text: In the event of failure of the braking distribution control, the vehicle shall stop under Type-0 conditions with engine disconnected with a stopping distance not exceeding 0.1 v + 0.0100 v² and a mean fully developed deceleration not less than 3.86 m/s².

requirements.quote: Initial brake temperature: Between 65 °C and 100 °C average on the hottest axle.
requirements.text: The wheel-lock sequence test shall be conducted with an initial brake temperature between 65 °C and 100 °C average on the hottest axle.

requirements.quote: Test speed: 65 km/h for a braking rate ≤ 0.50; 100 km/h for a braking rate > 0.50.
requirements.text: The wheel-lock sequence test shall be conducted at 65 km/h for a braking rate ≤ 0.50 and at 100 km/h for a braking rate > 0.50.

requirements.quote: Sample rate: All data acquisition and recording equipment shall support a minimum sample rate of 40 Hz on all channels.
requirements.text: All data acquisition and recording equipment for the torque wheel test shall support a minimum sample rate of 40 Hz on all channels.

requirements.quote: Any electrical failure or sensor anomaly that affects the system with respect to the functional and performance requirements in this annex shall be signalled to the driver by a specific optical warning signal.
requirements.text: Any electrical failure or sensor anomaly affecting the anti-lock system with respect to the functional and performance requirements shall be signalled to the driver by the yellow warning signal specified in paragraph 5.2.21.1.2.

requirements.quote: Sensor anomalies, which cannot be detected under static conditions, shall be detected not later than when the vehicle speed exceed 10 km/h.
requirements.text: Sensor anomalies of the anti-lock system which cannot be detected under static conditions shall be detected not later than when the vehicle speed exceeds 10 km/h.

requirements.quote: the subsequent service braking performance shall not be less than 80 per cent of the prescribed performance according to the Type-0 test with the engine disconnected.
requirements.text: In the event of a single electrical functional failure affecting only the anti-lock function, the subsequent service braking performance shall not be less than 80 per cent of the prescribed Type-0 performance, corresponding to a mean fully developed deceleration of 5.15 m/s².

requirements.quote: The operation of the anti-lock system shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields.
requirements.text: The operation of the anti-lock system used by the AEBS shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields, demonstrated by compliance with Regulation No. 10.

requirements.quote: The anti-lock system shall be deemed to be satisfactory when the condition ε ≥ 0.75 is satisfied, where ε represents the adhesion utilized
requirements.text: The anti-lock system shall be deemed satisfactory when the adhesion utilized ε is at least 0.75.

requirements.quote: The wheels directly controlled by an anti-lock system shall not lock when the full force8 is suddenly applied on the control device, on the road surfaces specified in paragraph 5.2.2. of this annex, at an initial speed of v = 40 km/h and at a high initial speed v = 0.8 vmax ≤ 120 km/h
requirements.text: The wheels directly controlled by the anti-lock system shall not lock when full force is suddenly applied at an initial speed of 40 km/h and at a high initial speed of 0.8 vmax ≤ 120 km/h.

requirements.quote: When an axle passes from a high-adhesion surface (kH) to a low-adhesion surface (kL), where kH ≥ 0.5 and kH / kL ≥ 2,10 with the full force8 applied on the control device, the directly controlled wheels shall not lock.
requirements.text: When an axle passes from a high-adhesion surface to a low-adhesion surface where kH ≥ 0.5 and kH / kL ≥ 2 with full force applied, the directly controlled wheels shall not lock.

requirements.quote: brief periods of wheel-locking shall be allowed. Furthermore, wheel-locking is permitted when the vehicle speed is less than 15 km/h
requirements.text: During the additional anti-lock checks, brief periods of wheel-locking shall be allowed and wheel-locking is permitted when the vehicle speed is less than 15 km/h, provided stability and steerability are not affected and the yaw angle does not exceed 15°.

requirements.quote: The value of ε shall be rounded to two decimal places.
requirements.text: The adhesion utilized value ε shall be rounded to two decimal places.

requirements.quote: The dynamometer shall be set as close as possible, with ±5 per cent tolerance, to the rotary inertia equivalent to that part of the total inertia of the vehicle braked by the appropriate wheel(s)
requirements.text: The inertia dynamometer for brake lining comparison shall be set within ±5 per cent of the rotary inertia equivalent to that part of the total inertia of the vehicle braked by the appropriate wheels.

requirements.quote: The velocity of the cooling air flowing over the brake shall be not greater than 10 km/h. The temperature of the cooling air shall be the ambient temperature.
requirements.text: The cooling air flowing over the brake during the dynamometer test shall have a velocity not greater than 10 km/h and a temperature equal to ambient temperature.

requirements.quote: Five sample sets of the brake lining shall be subjected to the comparison test; they shall be compared with five sets of linings conforming to the original components
requirements.text: Five sample sets of the brake lining shall be subjected to the comparison test, compared with five sets of linings conforming to the original components.

requirements.quote: The mean braking torque recorded during the above cold performance tests on the linings being tested for the purpose of comparison shall, for the same input measurement, be within the test limits ±15 per cent
requirements.text: The mean braking torque of the tested brake linings in the cold performance test shall, for the same input measurement, be within ±15 per cent of that of the original linings.

requirements.quote: Each unit shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.
requirements.text: Each braking system unit shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content.

requirements.quote: In case of a failure, the driver shall be warned for example by warning signal or message display.
requirements.text: The braking system shall warn the driver by warning signal or message display in case of a failure.

requirements.quote: The reaction of "the system" shall be checked under the influence of a failure in any individual unit by applying corresponding output signals to electrical units or mechanical elements in order to simulate the effects of internal faults within the unit.
requirements.text: The braking system reaction shall be checked under the influence of a failure in any individual unit by applying corresponding output signals to electrical units or mechanical elements to simulate internal faults.

requirements.quote: The sample(s) shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
requirements.text: The AEBS electrical/electronic sub-assembly sample shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.

requirements.quote: An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. below shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.
requirements.text: The AEBS electrical/electronic sub-assembly shall bear an approval mark described in paragraph 5.3 affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.

requirements.quote: A circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.text: The EMC approval mark on the AEBS ESA shall comprise a circle containing the letter E followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.

requirements.quote: Markings on ESAs in conformity with paragraph 5.3. above need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
requirements.text: The EMC approval marking on the AEBS ESA need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.

requirements.quote: A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.text: The AEBS and its electrical/electronic sub-assemblies shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the EMC requirements.

requirements.quote: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the limits shall be 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band and 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band
requirements.text: The vehicle fitted with the AEBS shall not exceed a broadband radiated emission of 32 dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz, 32 to 43 dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz increasing logarithmically, and 43 dBµV/m from 400 to 1000 MHz at a 10 m antenna spacing.

requirements.quote: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the limits shall be 28 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band and 35 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
requirements.text: The vehicle fitted with the AEBS shall not exceed a narrowband radiated emission of 28 dBµV/m from 30 to 230 MHz and 35 dBµV/m from 230 to 1000 MHz at a 10 m antenna spacing.

requirements.quote: the field strength shall be 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band
requirements.text: The vehicle fitted with the AEBS shall withstand a radiated immunity field strength of 30 V/m over 90 per cent and a minimum of 25 V/m over the whole 20 to 2000 MHz band, and 10 V/m over 90 per cent and a minimum of 8 V/m over the whole 2000 to 6000 MHz band.

requirements.quote: The vehicle representative of its type shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 6, there shall be no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions"
requirements.text: The AEBS shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity related functions during the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 6.

requirements.quote: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA shall not exceed a broadband radiated emission of 62 to 52 dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz decreasing logarithmically, 52 to 63 dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz increasing logarithmically and 63 dBµV/m from 400 to 1000 MHz.

requirements.quote: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA shall not exceed a narrowband radiated emission of 52 to 42 dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz decreasing logarithmically, 42 to 53 dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz increasing logarithmically and 53 dBµV/m from 400 to 1000 MHz.

requirements.quote: Table 1 Maximum allowed pulse amplitude
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA on a 24 V supply system shall not exceed a positive transient pulse amplitude of +150 V and a negative transient pulse amplitude of −450 V on its supply lines.

requirements.quote: Test Level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA shall withstand radiated immunity test levels of 60 V/m in stripline, 75 V/m in TEM cell, 60 mA in BCI and 30 V/m in ALSE over 90 per cent of the frequency range below 2 GHz, and 10 V/m in ALSE above 2 GHz.

requirements.quote: The ESA representative of its type shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity related functions during the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

requirements.quote: Test pulse number
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 at −450 V for 500 pulses with functional status classification III, and test pulses 2a at +37 V, 2b at +20 V, 3a at −150 V and 3b at +150 V with the functional performance status classifications specified for a 24 V system.

requirements.quote: Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2.
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA shall be deemed to comply with the narrowband emission limits where it does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz.

requirements.quote: The above approval mark affixed to a vehicle or ESA shows that the vehicle type concerned has, with regard to electromagnetic compatibility, been approved in the Netherlands (E 4) pursuant to Regulation No. 10
requirements.text: The EMC approval mark on the AEBS ESA shall have a minimum dimension a = 6 mm.

requirements.quote: The limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).
requirements.text: The broadband radiated emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure or an outdoor test site.

requirements.quote: Spectrum analyser parameters
requirements.text: The emission measurement spectrum analyser shall use a resolution bandwidth of 100/120 kHz at −3 dB with a minimum scan time of 100 ms/MHz for peak detection and 120 kHz at −6 dB with 20 s/MHz for quasi-peak detection in the 30 to 1000 MHz range.

requirements.quote: Measurements shall be made on the left and right sides of the vehicle.
requirements.text: The radiated emission measurements of the AEBS vehicle shall be made on the left and right sides of the vehicle, with the antenna positions documented in the test report.

requirements.quote: The vehicle's electronic systems shall all be in normal operating mode with the vehicle stationary.
requirements.text: For the narrowband emission measurement, all AEBS electronic systems shall be in normal operating mode with the vehicle stationary and the ignition switch on.

requirements.quote: Measurements shall be performed with an average detector.
requirements.text: The narrowband radiated emission measurements of the vehicle shall be performed with an average detector.

requirements.quote: Vehicle speed 50 km/h (respectively 25 km/h for L1, L2 vehicles) ±20 per cent (vehicle driving the rollers).
requirements.text: The AEBS vehicle immunity test shall be run in the 50 km/h mode with the vehicle speed at 50 km/h ±20 per cent on the dynamometer, with the speed maintained without deactivation where a cruise control is used.

requirements.quote: Brake pedal not depressed
requirements.text: During the 50 km/h immunity mode, depression of the brake pedal and unexpected activation of the stop lights shall constitute a failure criterion for the AEBS vehicle.

requirements.quote: Cluster operate in normal mode
requirements.text: The instrument cluster of the AEBS vehicle shall operate in normal mode during the immunity test, and unexpected warning or inconsistent variation of the odometer shall constitute a failure.

requirements.quote: Only non-perturbing equipment shall be used while monitoring the vehicle. The vehicle exterior and the passenger compartment shall be monitored to determine whether the requirements of this Annex are met
requirements.text: The AEBS vehicle immunity test shall be monitored with only non-perturbing equipment, with the vehicle exterior and passenger compartment monitored by video camera or microphone.

requirements.quote: The vehicle shall be exposed to electromagnetic radiation in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges in vertical polarization.
requirements.text: The AEBS vehicle shall be exposed to electromagnetic radiation in the 20 to 6000 MHz frequency range in vertical polarization.

requirements.quote: AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range
requirements.text: The immunity test signal shall be amplitude modulated with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range and pulse modulated with PM2 in 2700 to 3100 MHz and PM3 in 380 to 2700 MHz and 3100 to 6000 MHz.

requirements.quote: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA under broadband emission test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

requirements.quote: the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.5.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
requirements.text: The ambient extraneous noise or signal during the AEBS ESA emission measurement shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.5.2.1.

requirements.quote: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA under narrowband emission test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

requirements.quote: The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA under immunity test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition.

requirements.quote: Measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.

requirements.quote: Apply the test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA shall be subjected to test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 on its supply lines and on other connections operationally connected to supply lines.

requirements.quote: Apply the starting profile according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 to the supply lines
requirements.text: The AEBS ESA shall be subjected to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 on its supply lines where it may be installed in a vehicle with a 12 V/24 V starter motor.
